records.context: Study question Among women undergoing IVF, does embryo selection using non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing (niPGT) improve live birth and other clinical outcomes compared with conventional embryo selection? records.title: Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Aneuploidy Versus Morphological Selection in Women Aged 35–42: Results of a Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
records.authors: Yusuf Beebeejaun, Daniela N. Bakalova, Anastasia Mania, Timothy P. Copeland
records.context: Background/Objectives: Embryo selection in IVF is traditionally based on morphology, yet many high-quality embryos fail to implant. Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) using next-generation sequencing (NGS) has been proposed to improve selection by identifying euploid embryos. However, its effectiveness in women of advanced maternal age remains unclear due to limited randomized data. This pilot trial assessed the feasibility of a full-scale RCT comparing PGT-A to morphology-based selection in women aged 35-42. Methods: This single-centre, two-arm parallel RCT (NCT05009745) enrolled women aged 35-42 undergoing IVF/ICSI with ≥3 good-quality day-3 embryos. records.title: Invasive versus non-invasive PGT-A: A retrospective comparative study of embryo selection and IVF outcomes in women with recurrent IVF failure
records.journal: International Journal of Clinical Obstetrics and Gynaecology
records.context: Background: Recurrent IVF failure remains a significant clinical challenge, frequently attributed to embryonic aneuploidy. While invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) via trophectoderm biopsy is well established, non-invasive PGT-A using cell-free DNA from spent blastocyst culture media has emerged as a promising alternative. However, real-world comparative outcome data remain limited. Objective: To compare embryo assessment and clinical pregnancy outcomes between invasive and non-invasive PGT-A in women with recurrent IVF failure. Materials and Methods: This retrospective comparative study included 50 IVF cycles (30 invasive PGT-A, 20 non-invasive PGT-A) conducted from January 2023 to December 2024 at a single tertiary IVF centre. Women aged >30 years with ?2 failed IVF cycles, normal hysteroscopic findings, hormonal profile, and endometrial parameters were included.

records.title: Cell-free DNA in human ovarian follicular fluid as a potential biomarker of embryo quality in IVF cycles: a pilot study
records.authors: Eun-Hye Jo, Tae Hyung Kim, Jin Hee EUM, Jihye Jeong
records.context: IntroductionThere is growing interest in evaluating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in follicular fluid (FF) as a molecular feature of the follicular microenvironment and examining its association with subsequent embryo development. This exploratory pilot study aimed to investigate the association between FF cfDNA integrity, measured by the Arthrobacter luteus (ALU) 247/115 ratio, and morphology-based embryo quality in IVF cycles.MethodsThis observational study analyzed 106 follicular fluid samples from patients undergoing IVF with intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) at a single fertility center. FF samples were collected during ovum pick-up, and cfDNA concentrations were quantified using ALU-quantitative PCR. To evaluate the ALU247/115 ratio in relation to age, participants were categorized into three age groups.ResultsThe ALU247/115 ratio showed a significant but weak positive correlation with embryo quality score across all patients (n = 106, r = 0.23, p = 0.016). Subgroup analysis revealed stronger correlations in women under 35 years (n = 31, r = 0.38, p = 0.035) and those aged 35–39 years (n =40, r = 0.32, p = 0.044). No significant correlation was observed in women aged 40 or older (n = 35, r = 0.21, p = 0.225).ConclusionsIn women under 40, increased cfDNA fragmentation in FF was associated with lower morphology-based embryo quality. However, the observed correlations were modest, and the absence of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth outcomes limits clinical interpretation. These exploratory findings do not establish FF cfDNA as a clinically validated predictive biomarker or demonstrate that it improves embryo selection. Larger prospective studies incorporating embryo ploidy and clinically relevant reproductive outcomes are warranted.

records.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
records.context: Background: Thalassemia is a common autosomal recessive disorder that may impact reproductive health and embryo development. However, limited information is available regarding the impact of thalassemia carrier status on embryo euploidy, developmental competence, and embryo availability. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate the effects on women with thalassemia by analyzing data from women undergoing IVF with PGT-A.
